neet_phy_u12_t10_1.working: Rearranging P/Q = R/S gives S = RQ/P = 6×8/4 = 12 Ω.

neet_phy_u12_t10_2.working: AB/BC = 2/4 and AD/DC = 3/6, so the bridge is balanced and the 10 Ω resistor carries no current. Path ABC = 6 Ω and path ADC = 9 Ω in parallel give 54/15 = 3.6 Ω.

neet_phy_u12_t10_3.working: Doubling both P and S changes the condition to 2P/Q vs R/(2S), which is no longer equal, so the balance is disturbed. Changing the emf, swapping the cell and galvanometer, or changing the galvanometer resistance keeps the balance.

neet_phy_u12_t10_4.working: A is true: the balance condition involves only the four arm resistances. R is true: sensitivity is greatest when the resistances are of the same order. R is about sensitivity, so it does not explain A.

neet_phy_u12_t10_5.working: I: 10/20 = 15/30, so the bridge is balanced and no current flows in the galvanometer arm. Shorting the 5 Ω resistor therefore changes nothing, so I is true. II: after the swap, 20/10 ≠ 15/30, so the bridge is unbalanced and II is false.
